You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Test setup and intent:
  - The test builds a CSVPrinter with CSVFormat.DEFAULT.withEscape(null) and prints a single value "\" (a backslash) as the first field in a record.
  - The assertion expects the writer to contain just "\" (no escaping and no quoting), i.e., minimal formatting should not alter a lone backslash when no escape character is configured.

- Call flow:
  - CSVPrinter.print(value) delegates to CSVFormat.print(value, out, newRecord), which then calls the private print(object, charSequence, offset, len, out, newRecord).
  - In print(...):
    - Since this is the first value in a record (newRecord == true), and the object is not null, the code checks which formatting path to use:
      - Because the quote character is set in DEFAULT, isQuoteCharacterSet() is true, so it chooses printAndQuote(...).
      - The escape path (printAndEscape) is not used because withEscape(null) sets escapeCharacter to null and isEscapeCharacterSet() would be false.

- The quoting decision in MINIMAL mode:
  - In printAndQuote(...), when QuoteMode is MINIMAL, the code evaluates the first character of the value to decide whether to quote.
  - The relevant condition is:
    - if (newRecord && (c < '0' || (c > '9' && c < 'A') || (c > 'Z' && c < 'a') || (c > 'z'))) { quote = true; }
  - For the backslash character '\' (ASCII 92), at the start of a new record:
    - It satisfies (c > 'Z' && c < 'a') because 92 > 90 and 92 < 97, so quote is set to true.
  - As a result, the method wraps the backslash in quotes, producing "\"\"" (quote, backslash, quote), instead of leaving it as "\".

- Why this is a bug relative to the test and the issue report:
  - The test’s expectation is that with no escape character configured, a single backslash at the start of a record should not be quoted in MINIMAL mode.
  - The unexpected quoting arises from the “first-character” rule in MINIMAL mode that forces quoting of any first character outside [0-9A-Za-z], regardless of whether it is actually necessary under typical CSV minimal quoting semantics (which usually quote only when encountering delimiter, quote, CR/LF, or leading/trailing spaces).
  - This same rule also explains the reported issue about negative numbers in the first column being quoted: a leading '-' is not alphanumeric, so the rule forces quoting in the first column in MINIMAL mode.

- Root cause:
  - The heuristic in CSVFormat.printAndQuote(...) for MINIMAL mode that quotes any first field whose first character is non-alphanumeric when newRecord == true. This legacy rule causes unnecessary quoting for:
    - Negative numbers in the first column (leading '-').
    - A lone backslash in the first column (this test).
  - The correct behavior for MINIMAL mode should base quoting on the presence of delimiter, quote, CR/LF, or leading/trailing spaces, not on “non-alphanumeric first character” at the start of a record.

In short, the failing test and the reported negative-number behavior both stem from the same condition in MINIMAL mode inside printAndQuote(...): the first-character rule that forces quoting at the start of a record for non-alphanumeric characters.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
CSVFormat.printAndQuote(java.lang.Object, java.lang.CharSequence, int, int, java.lang.Appendable, boolean)
